tweets.text:
🇩🇪🇺🇦 Germany has changed its position and now supports the use of frozen Russian assets to finance Ukraine's needs — Bloomberg.

Germany's previously cautious position on asset seizures has recently changed, in part due to concerns that if the United States completely stops aid to Ukraine, the burden of supporting Kyiv would fall disproportionately on Berlin.

The various options do not include a full seizure of assets, which is supported by the United States and some European countries. According to Bloomberg sources, the issue of obtaining additional income from the assets is planned to be discussed at a meeting of EU finance ministers in Copenhagen this week, as well as at a summit of EU leaders in October.

A final decision is expected to be made during the EU leaders' summit on October 23-24.

Ukraine is currently receiving funds from frozen Russian assets under the G7 mechanism, which provided Ukraine with a $50 billion loan financed by windfall profits from these assets.
